brief: Speculators are hesitant to go fully risk-on because of the risk of higher yields, leaving markets at an impasse. Stocks cannot break to new highs without a new positive narrative, and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra release did not supply one. Yields stay elevated for good reasons (rising real growth expectations, reinforced by Friday's positive jobs data, and heavy AI-related investment) and bad reasons (fiscal incontinence and inflation). Speculator positioning in risk-on assets (Bitcoin, AUD, NZD, BRL, MXN, CAD) versus risk-off assets (JPY, CHF, DXY, gold, VIX) is net flat as of Tuesday last week, reflecting reluctance to commit fully while uncertainty persists. The jobs data probably adds some impetus for yields to rise further, though seasonality may cap the rise before year-end. Two data points flag rising yield risk: JPMorgan's Treasury client survey shows more shorts, and Treasury ETF outflows have jumped to a rarely seen level. Because IEF and TLT short interest has held steady, the outflows are read as genuine selling rather than short-covering. If the market is starting to price in appreciably higher yields, that would explain the reticence to go risk-on.
